outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms are possible this afternoon and evening across the lower Great Lakes region and Ohio Valley into parts of the Northeast, accompanied mainly by the risk for damaging wind gusts. A tornado threat also exists today from Pennsylvania into eastern New York and western Vermont. Scattered strong thunderstorms may also impact parts of the Ozark Plateau into the south central Plains, with at least some risk for severe weather.

sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: An upper trough centered over northern Ontario/Upper Great Lakes at 12Z today is expected to deepen and evolve into a closed low as it shifts east into southern Quebec. Strengthening cyclonic flow regime is expected from the upper MS Valley through the OH Valley to the Northeast States this forecast period, with mid-level impulses embedded in this flow spreading across the OH Valley to the Northeast. Farther to the southwest, impulses of monsoonal origin will spread from NM into the southern Plains, while additional impulses migrate from the southern Great Basin to the central Rockies region. At the surface, substantial cyclogenesis is expected across Quebec in response to the approaching deepening closed low aloft. A trailing cold front will advance to the southeast and south into the OH Valley, Ozarks and southern Plains this afternoon, and into the Northeast States tonight to early Wednesday morning. Ahead of this front, a warm, humid airmass will exist and support development of numerous showers and thunderstorms in mainly multiple bands from midday onward across the OH Valley and Northeast and west/southwestward into the southern Plains.

sections.title: Northeast States to the OH Valley
sections.text: Rich moisture (precipitable water ranging from 1.5-2.0 inches) is expected to spread to the east/northeast across the rest of the OH Valley into the Northeast States this forecast period contributing to strong destabilization, especially from the OH Valley into southern PA. Farther north into northern PA, NY to western New England, there remains some uncertainty with the degree of overall destabilization, partly due to weak mid-level lapse rates. However, stronger forcing for ascent expected across NY into New England may prove sufficient to compensate for weaker instability and support organized line segments spreading to the east as deep-layer westerly shear vectors strengthen (effective bulk shear at 35-45 kt). A linear storm mode should be predominate with damaging winds expected as deep-layer winds strengthen, including 40-50 kt at 850-700 mb, with the greatest threat occurring from northern PA into central and eastern NY. Given the deepening surface low into Quebec this afternoon, low-level winds from eastern PA to eastern NY should remained backed, enhancing low-level shear for a tornado threat (especially with any discrete storms).

sections.title: Southern Plains eastward to Missouri/Arkansas
sections.text: This region will remain displaced from stronger mid/upper flow associated with the Canadian/Northeast U.S. trough, resulting in mainly weak deep-layer shear. Despite this factor, strong instability is expected in response to strong surface heating within a moist environment (precipitable water ranging from 1.75 to 2+ inches). Forcing for ascent with the cold front and attendant to several weak impulses shifting to the east/southeast across these areas suggest scattered thunderstorms should develop with at least an isolated risk for hail and damaging downburst winds. These storms could evolve into one or two loosely organized clusters before weakening during the evening. ..Peters/Gleason.. 08/22/2017

outlooks.summary: Severe thunderstorms with damaging winds, and possibly a couple of tornadoes, are expected this afternoon from the upper Ohio Valley to Pennsylvania and New York. Thunderstorms with isolated strong/damaging gusts will also be possible farther southwest into parts of the southern Plains.

sections.title: NY/PA to the southern Plains through late evening
sections.text: A pronounced midlevel trough over the upper Great Lakes will continue to amplify while approaching Quebec tonight. Associated surface cyclogenesis preceding the midlevel trough will drive a surface cold front southeastward across the lower Great Lakes and OH Valley by tonight. In addition, the remnants of a subtropical speed max, enhanced by overnight convection across IL/MO, will accelerate east-northeastward over the OH Valley/PA/NY in advance of the primary midlevel trough, and in phase with the diurnal heating cycle. It appears that the primary focus for thunderstorm development today will a pre-frontal or the remnant outflow/differential heating zone on the leading edge of the ongoing convection from IN to MO. Convection will likely strengthen/redevelop by midday or early afternoon across OH and western NY, and storms will subsequently spread eastward across PA/NY through the afternoon. Midlevel flow and effective bulk shear will likewise strengthen into the 40-50 kt range from OH to PA/NY this afternoon, as surface heating results in steepening low-level lapse rates and MLCAPE near 1500 J/kg. outlooks.summary: Scattered to numerous swaths of damaging winds are expected from the Ohio Valley to western New England through this evening. A couple tornadic storms are possible, mainly over parts of New York into Pennsylvania.

sections.title: THERE IS AN ENHANCED RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS NY/PA
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OH VALLEY TO WESTERN NEW ENGLAND... ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS SOUTHERN HIGH PLAINS TO NEW ENGLAND...

sections.title: OH Valley to western New England
sections.text: Minimal change necessary this outlook with numerous storms expected to develop in the next few hours. A pronounced shortwave trough over the Upper Great Lakes will continue to amplify while approaching Quebec tonight. Associated surface cyclogenesis will drive a cold front southeast across the Lower Great Lakes and OH Valley. Primary focus for storm development will be along the remnant outflow/differential heating zone ahead of the front. Strong tropospheric winds will support effective shear of 30-40 kt southwest to 40-50 kt northeast. In spite of poor mid-level lapse rates, robust diabatic heating will contribute to MLCAPE of 1500-2500 J/kg southwest to 1000-2000 J/kg northeast. An initially mixed mode should transition to line segments with swaths of damaging winds expected, especially with bowing segments. Stronger low-level shear and enlarged hodographs are expected across parts of NY into northern PA. Although storm mode may limit the sustenance of rotating updrafts, embedded QLCS mesovortices should support a threat for a couple tornadoes. For additional short-term discussion, please see MCDs 1547 and 1548.

sections.title: Southern High Plains to Mid-South
sections.text: Deep-layer flow and shear will be substantially weaker along a southward-sagging cold front and pre-frontal outflow near the I-40 corridor. Loosely organized multicell clusters are expected mid-afternoon to mid-evening with isolated downbursts and marginally severe hail possible. ..Grams/Cohen.. 08/22/2017

outlooks.summary: Scattered to numerous swaths of damaging winds are expected from the Ohio Valley to parts of New England through the early overnight. A couple tornadic storms are possible, mainly from northern Pennsylvania to northern New England. Bands of strong/severe convection have organized from Upstate New York southwestward to the Ohio Valley this afternoon, fueled by sufficient boundary-layer destabilization and surface dew points in the mid 60s to lower 70s. Aided by broad ascent within the cyclonic flow regime aloft, these storms should continue east/northeastward into the evening. Additionally, a few more organized segments may persist well into the late evening and early overnight, as nocturnal cooling should be limited some by a moist boundary layer. Meanwhile, the surface cyclone over Quebec will further deepen, owing to the approach of a vigorous shortwave trough over the upper Great Lakes currently. Surface to 700 mb south/southwesterly flow will amplify in response to the deepening system, and low-level shear should increase considerably as well across much of western and northern New England. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe thunderstorm watch will likely be issued by 17z across portions of the Ohio Valley.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Pre-frontal boundary-layer cumulus field is expanding/deepening across the OH Valley as surface temperatures warm into the lower 80s. While mid-level lapse rates are poor due to high PW air mass, surface-3km lapse rates have steepened enough for surface parcels to reach their LFC. Lightning is beginning to increase with maturing convection from the northwest portions of PA, southwest along the OH River into southern IN. This activity should gradually increase in areal coverage within a sheared environment favorable for organized line segments and clusters. A considerable amount of convection is expected along this corridor within a few hours and locally damaging winds can be expected with these storms. Severe thunderstorm watch is warranted for this evolving threat.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The risk for severe thunderstorms with damaging winds and tornadoes is increasing, and the severe risk will continue through the afternoon. The issuance of a Tornado Watch will be forthcoming within the next couple of hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Large-scale forcing for ascent continues atop a relatively moist boundary layer characterized by upper 60s to lower 70s surface dewpoints. Pockets of at least modest insolation will continue to enhance buoyancy, with MLCAPE forecast to increase to 1000-1500 J/kg ahead of a pre-frontal trough/effective boundary crossing the Great Lakes region. Thunderstorms will continue to increase in coverage and intensity from western NY to western PA and spread eastward and northeastward through the afternoon, amidst weak capping. The presence of 30-40 kt of effective shear accompanying a mid-level speed maximum will promote organized convective structures, including quasi-linear segments and perhaps a few transient supercells. Moderate low-level shear in the warm sector associated with a low-level jet, enhanced by a trough-related deep cyclone north of the area, will support some tornado risk with cells and with meso-vortices embedded in lines, given 150-300 m2/s2 of effective SRH. Otherwise, damaging wind gusts will be likely -- enhanced with small, line-accompanying rear-inflow jets. A Tornado Watch will be issued.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe-thunderstorm and tornado risk continues across WW 461, and will spread east to northeast with time. The tornado risk may be increasing across parts of northern and central NY into western/northern New England, and areas east of WW 461 are being monitored for possible WW issuance later today.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: In association with ongoing cyclogenesis in western Quebec, observational trends suggest that pressure falls are increasing in magnitude across the area -- now up to around 3 mb per 2 hours -- focused within a corridor from north-central PA through central NY and northward into southern Quebec. This aligns with a strengthening low-level jet within the warm sector of the deepening cyclone. The mass response to the cyclogenesis process will continue to focus strengthening low-level shear from south-central NY through the Adirondacks vicinity and into western/northern parts of New England amid strengthening deep shear -- i.e. effective shear increasing upwards of 50 kt. With a sufficiently moist boundary layer and diurnal heating supporting 1250-1750 J/kg of MLCAPE, these factors will continue to support organizing convective clusters and occasional supercells -- a trend that has already been noted from western NY into northwest PA. The tornado risk will likely increase as this activity spreads eastward to northeastward amid the strengthening low-level and deep shear. Despite low-level shear vectors being oriented somewhat parallel-oblique to evolving convective lines, low-level SRH is strengthening and line-orthogonal deep shear is enhanced. Also, of particular note, the isallobaric response to the deepening surface cyclone is resulting in locally backed winds from northern NY into adjacent New England -- enhanced locally by terrain-induced flow channeling -- resulting in appreciable low-level hodograph curvature supporting around 300 m2/s2 of effective SRH. The ample streamwise vorticity within the convective inflow should boost the tornado risk. mesoscale_discussions.summary: Scattered bands of strong/severe thunderstorms will progress across WW462.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Multiple bands of strong/severe thunderstorms have evolved across the OH Valley this afternoon. This activity has matured within a corridor of stronger boundary-layer heating from KY, northeast into western PA. Additionally, there appears to be added ascent ahead of two long-lived remnant MCVs from over night convection. One MCV is located over north-central OH near MFD and the other is located over extreme southwest IN north of EVV. Each of these features may enhance the clustering potential of storms immediately downstream. Damaging winds appear to be the primary threat with convection this afternoon. ..Darrow.. 08/22/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorms will increase in number and intensity through late afternoon and continue into the evening with isolated severe potential. Present indications are that Watch issuance will be unlikely, though areas from the lower Ohio Valley to the mid-South will especially be monitored for somewhat relatively greater severe potential.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: An outflow boundary arcs from southern AR northeastward to the mid-South and intersects a deeper, synoptic, northeastward- extending, baroclinic zone near a triple point in the vicinity of the MO Bootheel. The warm-sector air mass is becoming strongly unstable owing to insolation amidst dewpoints in the 70s. Despite limited mid-level lapse rates, the favorably moist boundary layer is supporting ample MLCAPE -- around 2000-3500 J/kg -- which will yield robust updrafts developing along the modestly convergent aforementioned boundaries. As initial convective elements merge with amalgamating cold pools, locally damaging wind gusts may evolve -- particularly across the lower Ohio Valley and mid-South where effective shear upwards of 25 kt and DCAPE around 1000-1500 J/kg exist. Isolated severe hail could also accompany incipient intense updrafts. However, surface boundaries governing convective initiation have become largely dislodged to the south of stronger deep shear accompanying a mid-level speed maximum. Accordingly, the overall convective organization and severe risk should be limited.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will increase across the northern Middle Atlantic over the next several hours. Damaging winds are possible with convection that spreads into this region and a Severe Thunderstorm Watch will likely be issued by 20z.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Strong boundary-layer heating continues along a corridor from the Delmarva into the northern Middle Atlantic where temperatures have warmed through the mid 80s to near 90F. CU field is gradually deepening across the higher terrain of central PA/NY ahead of two distinct convective lines that are gradually maturing towards well-organized squall lines. The leading squall line will likely be the primary severe threat as it advances across the remainder of WWs 461/462 into a region of untapped instability characterized by MLCAPE on the order of 2000 J/kg. Given the large-scale support ahead of the upper trough these organized bands of convection should progress into the lower Hudson Valley and eastern PA by late afternoon.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated severe-thunderstorm risk is expected to exist into the late afternoon and early evening hours. Watch issuance will be unlikely.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: The following zones will be focus areas for convective deepening into the late afternoon hours: (1) an outflow boundary arcing from east-central OK toward the Tulsa area, (2) differential-heating-induced baroclinicity on the warm-side fringes of a multi-layered cloud band from the Wichita Falls and Lawton areas toward Norman and Tulsa, (3) modest synoptic frontal convergence from east-central NM into west-central OK (convectively influenced in NM), and (4) deeper baroclinicity along a stronger-frontal segment just south of the northeast OK/southeast KS border. Modifications to the 17Z and 18Z observed soundings across the area suggest that capping aloft continues to erode as pockets of at least filtered insolation continue on the warm sides of the aforementioned zones of convective initiation. Related convective inflow is becoming increasingly buoyant, with MLCAPE increasing to 1000-2500 J/kg -- highest magnitudes where insolation has been strongest. While pockets of ongoing clouds are locally muting diabatic surface-layer heating in parts of OK, eventually strengthening/expanding cold pools will likely breed growing convective coverage/intensity during the next few hours across the entire area, amid DCAPE upwards of 1000-1250 J/kg. Sporadic severe wind gusts may accompany collapsing convective cores into the evening hours, though weak effective shear will limit convective organization and severe coverage. The isolated severe risk will tend to spread southward with time owing to preferential growth of incipient updrafts into the more buoyant air with southward extent across the region.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat has shifted to areas mostly east of Ohio and south of the Ohio River.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Significant convective overturning has occurred across OH this afternoon with strongest storms having shifted to the east and south. Two primary lines of storms have evolved over WW462 with the eastern-most band extending from western PA into eastern KY. This line of storms has produced isolated damaging winds gusts and should continue to do so, especially the northern line segment, as it propagates toward central PA. The southwestern-most line segment along the OH River has struggled to generate severe wing gusts or damage. Even so, environmental shear remains supportive of convective organization and this band of storms should propagate across much of KY over the next several hours with some attendant wind threat. ..Darrow.. 08/22/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe-thunderstorm and tornado risk continues across WW 461. The greatest tornado risk will likely continue to focus across portions of eastern/northeastern NY over the next few hours.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar analysis shows a pair of eastward-moving QLCSs traversing NY/northern PA, with embedded bowing-line segments and transient supercell structures. Objective analysis continues to indicate the most favorable environment for a couple of tornadoes existing across eastern/northeastern NY, where locally backed surface flow is acting to elongate hodograph curvature leading to enhanced effective SRH values (e.g., at or above 200 m2/s2). While a brief tornado remains possible farther south across southern NY, slightly veered low-level flow across this area will tend to limit tornado potential. However, developing bowing radar-reflectivity structures suggest an increase damaging wind potential across this area.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: The severe-thunderstorm threat is expected to continue increasing across WW 463 this evening. Portions of the region will be monitored for possible new Tornado Watch issuance.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Radar imagery indicates a QLCS with embedded bowing segments and preceding supercell structures from northern and central NY to central PA. The environment across WW 463 is strongly sheared through a deep layer (e.g., near 50 kt of effective bulk-wind difference) and characterized by moderate instability (e.g., MLCAPE 1000-1500 J/kg). Furthermore, locally backed low-level flow is present from central and eastern NY into New England, which is associated with enhanced effective SRH values (e.g., 200-300 m2/s2). These factors suggest that the tornado threat continues, and may increase further in association with larger-scale cyclogenesis. Cells developing within a warm-advection corridor from near Binghamton to east-central NY may continue to mature into semi-discrete supercells with increased tornado potential -- potentially spreading into New England. This may especially be the case with convection spreading across the Hudson Valley region and vicinity, where terrain-channeled flow is more substantially boosting low-level streamwise vorticity. Otherwise, damaging winds remain likely with evolving QLCS segments across the Watch area, with the risk for a few line-embedded meso-vortices and possible tornadoes. If it were to appear that greater tornado risk were to evolve into parts of eastern NY and adjacent New England, new Tornado Watch issuance may become necessary.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A few storms may increase in intensity as they progress across eastern Pennsylvania and vicinity. Damaging winds, a brief/weak tornado, and marginal hail are all possible.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Surface analysis shows continued pressure falls across eastern PA, ahead of the main line of storms. In addition, this corridor currently is near the instability axis, with MLCAPE around 1500 J/kg. Deep-layer shear remains favorable for long-lived severe storms, roughly 45-50 kt and at a large angle to the front. 0-1 km SRH also remains favorable for supercells and/or a brief tornado at over 100 M2/s2. Recent radar trends have shown some increase in cells ahead of the line, and if this trend persists, some of these cells may turn right and become supercells, with threat of a brief tornado, hail, and damaging wind. ..Jewell.. 08/22/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: An isolated strong to damaging wind threat wind threat should continue with storms moving eastward across WW 463 this evening. A tornado or two may also occur.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent radar imagery depicts a broken line of storms along a pre-frontal trough moving eastward across much of New England. Strong low and mid-level winds veering with height will continue to support storm organization this evening, with latest RAP Mesoanalysis suggesting effective bulk shear values remain around 40-50 kt across this region. Even though diurnal cooling has commenced and mid-level lapse rates remain poor, a very moist low-level airmass is contributing to around 500 to locally 1500 J/kg of MLCAPE, sufficient to maintain ongoing storm intensities. Isolated instances of strong to locally damaging winds should remain the primary severe threat for the next several hours given the mainly linear nature of ongoing storms. A tornado or two may also occur with any supercell embedded within or just ahead of the short thunderstorm line segments, as strongly veering/strengthening low-level winds with height are resulting in effective SRH values of 200-275 m2/s2. The overall severe threat should gradually lessen later this evening as instability weakens further with the loss of daytime heating. ..Gleason.. 08/23/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong to damaging wind gusts remain possible this evening, but a general downward trend should persist. As such, new watches are not anticipated.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A line of storms currently extends from southwestern ME into eastern PA, with the strongest activity over PA and NJ. Here, instability is greater, and supercells have merged into a linear structure with congealing outflows. Some strong to damaging wind gusts remain possible along the entire length of the line due to strong mean-layer winds. The gradually cooling boundary layer and increasing CIN should allow for a downward trend in storm intensity. However, very heavy rain remains likely especially where storms movement is parallel to the flow. ..Jewell.. 08/23/2017 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
